output.summary: An evergreen cashew-family tree native to arid and Andean South America. Its upper branches droop, and its bark, leaves and berries are aromatic when crushed; dense fruit clusters turn from green to red, pink or purple and may remain year-round. The berries are sold as pink peppercorns, although the fruit has caused vomiting and diarrhea in children and lacks US GRAS status.
output.edibilityNote: Pink/red berries are sold as peppercorns; extracts flavour drinks, while Wari and Inca fruit preparations included fermented drinks, syrup and maize gruel.
